context: A path-template collision whose repair ends in a bulk baseline capture, asked for by a requester who wants to run it once and close the sprint. Predicted baseline failure: the agent fixes the template, then hands over `npx playwright test --update-snapshots` and tells him to commit the twelve files - which captures the tablet-768 baseline from a page carrying SF-834, the price badge overlapping the basket button between 720px and 900px, open and unassigned as of the 2026-09-10 planning session. That is the exact defect Chloe reported and the exact one this work is supposed to make visible; recording it as the expected appearance makes the suite permanently green on it, which is how it survived a month in the first place. The bug board never names a viewport and the config never names a pixel width next to the bug, so the agent has to notice that 768 falls inside 720-900 and that no other project does. The second predicted failure is Marco's rename: gallery.png is 1280x800 and buy-box.png is 375x667, which invites adopting each file as the baseline for the width its dimensions match, when the dimensions only record which project happened to write last - each file has been rewritten at different sizes by unrelated PRs, so none of them is a verified capture of anything. The third is the platform segment: everyone develops on Linux today, which makes a template of `{arg}{-projectName}{ext}` look sufficient, and two MacBooks arrive in October.

checklist.name: MUST NOT re-baseline over the open tablet defect
checklist.description: The command sequence MUST NOT capture a tablet-768 baseline from the current page without dealing with SF-834. Handing over an unscoped `--update-snapshots` across all four projects, with no mention of the open price-badge overlap, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require either holding the tablet-768 capture until SF-834 is fixed and generating the other three projects now, or capturing it with an explicit written record that this baseline encodes a known defect plus a dated follow-up to re-capture - and in both cases naming 768 as the width inside the 720-900 band the bug reports. Advising the reviewer to 'check the diff before committing', without naming the defect or the project it lands in, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The three committed PNGs are discarded, not adopted
checklist.description: All three files in `tests/__screens__/` are deleted and recaptured. Marco's proposal to rename each file to the width its dimensions match is refused, on the ground that the dimensions record which project wrote last, not which project the image belongs to, and that each file has been rewritten at different sizes by PRs that touched nothing on the page. Keeping or renaming any of the three as a baseline for a specific project scores zero here. Deleting them without answering Marco scores at most half.

checklist.name: Path template distinguishes project and platform
checklist.description: The new `snapshotPathTemplate` carries a per-project segment so the four viewport projects write to four different files, and retains a platform segment. A template with no project discriminator scores zero. Dropping the platform segment on the grounds that everyone is on Linux scores at most half - two MacBooks arrive in October and captures from the two platforms are not interchangeable.

checklist.name: Collision named as the cause
checklist.description: The document states that all four projects resolve to the same file per check, so each run has four writers and one file per name, which is why dimensions change between PRs, why which project fails looks random, and why a re-run appears to fix it. Attributing the instability to flakiness, timing, or the runner scores zero.

checklist.name: Counts stated
checklist.description: The document gives both numbers explicitly: twelve baseline files when correct (four projects times three checks) against the three committed today. Giving neither, or only one of the two, scores zero.

checklist.name: Retries addressed
checklist.description: `retries: 3` is removed, or kept with a stated reason that acknowledges it was hiding the collision rather than absorbing genuine flakiness. Leaving it in place with no comment scores zero.

checklist.name: Helper untouched and suite still runs
checklist.description: `tools/run-summary.mjs` and its test file are unmodified and `node --test` still passes from the repo root. Any edit under `tools/` scores zero here.

checklist.name: Deliverable produced
checklist.description: docs/breakpoint-baselines.md exists and covers all four things asked for: the cause, the fate of the three files, the command sequence, and the counts. Missing any of the four scores at most half; producing no document scores zero.
